components.note: 钅 (metal) — clocks and bells like 钟 were traditionally made of metal.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 钟.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 开车到那里大概要两个钟头。
example.pinyin: kāichē dào nàlǐ dàgài yào liǎng gè zhōngtóu.
example.english: Driving there takes about two hours.
example.fact: The mechanical escapement clock, invented in medieval Europe around the 14th century, was one of the first machines to divide time into equal, repeatable intervals — before that, most timekeeping relied on sundials or water clocks that varied with the seasons. This standardization of the hour eventually made synchronized schedules, and later factory shift work, possible on a mass scale.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
亻 (person) — 倍 relates to multiplying or doubling an amount, an action tied to people and quantities.
咅 (pǒu) is close in sound to bèi, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 如果不小心保管，损失可能会加倍。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ bù xiǎoxīn bǎoguǎn, sǔnshī kěnéng huì jiābèi.
example.english: If it's not handled carefully, the losses could double.
example.fact: Exponential doubling is deceptively powerful: a single sheet of paper folded 42 times would theoretically reach the Moon, because each fold doubles its thickness. This is the same principle behind Moore's Law, which observed that the number of transistors on a computer chip roughly doubled every two years for decades.

components.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'

example.hanzi: 她决定去做整容手术改变鼻子的形状。
example.pinyin: tā juédìng qù zuò zhěngróng shǒushù gǎibiàn bízi de xíngzhuàng.
example.english: She decided to have plastic surgery to change the shape of her nose.
example.fact: The first modern techniques for reconstructive facial surgery emerged from treating soldiers' injuries in World War I, when surgeon Harold Gillies pioneered skin-graft methods at a specialized hospital in Sidcup, England. Many of today's cosmetic surgery techniques trace their lineage directly back to those wartime reconstructive innovations.

components.note: 酉 (a wine vessel) — 配 originally related to blending or mixing wine
己 (jǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 配's reading pèi, having drifted apart over time
方 originally depicted the crossbar of a plow, or possibly two boats lashed side by side — the sense of a flat, regular shape later extended to 'direction' and 'method.'

example.hanzi: 这家饼店的配方已经保密了三十年。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā bǐngdiàn de pèifāng yǐjīng bǎomì le sānshí nián.
example.english: This bakery's recipe has been kept secret for thirty years.
example.fact: Coca-Cola's exact syrup formula is one of the most famous trade secrets in business history — the written recipe has reportedly been locked in a vault at the World of Coca-Cola museum in Atlanta since 2011, and only a small number of executives have ever known the complete formulation.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蚂 names a small crawling creature.

虫 (insect) — 蚁 names a small insect.
义 (yì) gives a sound close to yǐ, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 一只蚂蚁能搬动比自己重很多倍的食物。
example.pinyin: yì zhī mǎyǐ néng bāndòng bǐ zìjǐ zhòng hěn duō bèi de shíwù.
example.english: A single ant can carry food many times heavier than its own body.
example.fact: Ants can collectively outweigh every wild mammal on Earth combined — a 2022 study estimated the total ant population at around 20 quadrillion individuals, with a combined dry biomass exceeding that of all wild birds and mammals put together. Their colonies also function as 'superorganisms,' coordinating complex behavior with no central leader.

components.note: 阝 (from 邑, a settlement) — 那 was originally the name of an ancient state or place.

土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 那场雨下得特别大，街道全都被淹了。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng yǔ xià de tèbié dà, jiēdào quán dōu bèi yān le.
example.english: That rainstorm was especially heavy, and the streets were all flooded.
example.fact: The wettest 24-hour rainfall ever recorded on Earth occurred on Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean in January 1966, when tropical cyclone rainfall dumped about 1,825 millimeters — over 71 inches — of rain in a single day, more than many cities receive in a year.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他这次考试的分数比上次高了很多。
example.pinyin: tā zhè cì kǎoshì de fēnshù bǐ shàng cì gāo le hěn duō.
example.english: His score on this exam was much higher than last time.
example.fact: The practice of grading student work with a percentage score is a relatively recent invention — Yale is often credited with introducing a numerical grading scale in the 1780s, while the now-familiar A-through-F letter grade system wasn't standardized in American schools until the early 20th century.

臼 (jiù) gives the sound — an exact match with 舅.

example.hanzi: 我舅舅每年过年都会给我压岁钱。

example.english: My maternal uncle gives me New Year's money every year during the holiday.
example.fact: In many matrilineal societies, such as the Mosuo of southwestern China, a mother's brother traditionally plays a larger role in raising children than the biological father does, since family lineage and property pass down through the mother's side rather than the father's.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.

example.hanzi: 弟弟趁妈妈不注意，偷看了礼物的包装。
example.pinyin: dìdi chèn māma bú zhùyì, tōukàn le lǐwù de bāozhuāng.
example.english: My little brother snuck a peek at the wrapped gift while Mom wasn't looking.
example.fact: The 'Zeigarnik effect,' named after psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik who studied it in the 1920s, describes how unfinished or hidden information — like a wrapped present — creates a persistent mental itch, making people far more likely to remember and think about it than something already fully revealed.

components.note: 欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他们周末去剧院看了一场意大利歌剧。
example.pinyin: tāmen zhōumò qù jùyuàn kàn le yì chǎng Yìdàlì gējù.
example.english: They went to the theater over the weekend to watch an Italian opera.
example.fact: Opera originated in Florence, Italy, around 1600, when a group of humanist scholars and musicians called the Florentine Camerata tried to revive what they believed was ancient Greek musical drama. Their earliest surviving example, Jacopo Peri's 'Euridice,' is considered the first opera whose complete score has survived to today.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
木 (tree) — relates directly to 根's meaning 'root (of a plant or tree).'
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 根 is pronounced gēn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: J.P.摩根是十九世纪美国最有影响力的银行家之一。
example.pinyin: J.P. Mó gēn shì shíjiǔ shìjì Měiguó zuì yǒu yǐngxiǎnglì de yínhángjiā zhī yī.
example.english: J.P. Morgan was one of the most influential bankers in 19th-century America.
example.fact: J.P. Morgan personally organized a private bailout of the U.S. Treasury in 1895, using his own banking syndicate's gold reserves to replenish the federal government's gold supply during a financial panic — an act of private intervention in the national economy that would be almost unthinkable today.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'

弗 (fú) gives a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

example.hanzi: 这个停车场晚上十点以后不收费。
example.pinyin: zhège tíngchēchǎng wǎnshang shí diǎn yǐhòu bù shōufèi.
example.english: This parking lot doesn't charge a fee after 10 p.m.
example.fact: The world's first toll roads date back to ancient times — a stretch of road near Susa in Iran shows evidence of a toll gate from around 2700 BC, and the Roman Empire later formalized toll collection to help fund the vast network of roads connecting its territories.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僵 describes a person's body becoming stiff.
畺 (jiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 僵.
石 (stone) — 硬 describes something as hard and firm as stone.
更 (gèng) gives a sound distantly related to yìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 长时间坐着让他的肩膀变得僵硬。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān zuòzhe ràng tā de jiānbǎng biàn de jiāngyìng.
example.english: Sitting for a long time made his shoulders stiff.
example.fact: Rigor mortis, the stiffening of muscles after death, is caused by a buildup of calcium ions inside muscle cells once the body stops producing ATP — the molecule that normally lets muscle fibers release their grip. It typically sets in within a few hours and fades again within one to three days as the tissue begins to break down.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 学校每个学期都会安排一次消防演习。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào měi gè xuéqī dōu huì ānpái yí cì xiāofáng yǎnxí.
example.english: The school arranges a fire drill once every semester.
example.fact: The largest peacetime military exercise series during the Cold War, NATO's 'Reforger,' at times involved moving well over 100,000 troops and their equipment across the Atlantic to Europe, testing how quickly the alliance could reinforce its defenses if war broke out.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 束 depicts a bundle of wood.

example.english: Traditional attitudes often constrain people's choices.
example.fact: Straitjackets, perhaps the most literal embodiment of being physically bound, were first introduced in 18th-century French asylums as an alternative to chains and were originally seen as a humane innovation — though by the 20th century they had become a symbol of the harsh restraint methods psychiatric institutions later moved away from.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
几 traces the outline of a simple stand or tray.

example.hanzi: 他过着平凡却充实的生活。
example.pinyin: tā guò zhe píngfán què chōngshí de shēnghuó.
example.english: He lives an ordinary but fulfilling life.
example.fact: The 'Blue Marble' photograph of Earth, taken by the crew of Apollo 17 in 1972, shows a small, ordinary-looking blue and white sphere against the blackness of space — yet it became one of the most reproduced images in history and helped catalyze the modern environmental movement by making the planet's fragility visible.

皮 (pí) gives a sound close to 波's reading bō, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 肖邦是波兰最著名的作曲家之一。
example.pinyin: Xiāobāng shì Bōlán zuì zhùmíng de zuòqǔjiā zhī yī.
example.english: Chopin is one of Poland's most famous composers.
example.fact: Poland's borders have shifted dramatically over history — in the late 18th century the country was completely partitioned and erased from the map by Russia, Prussia, and Austria for 123 years, only regaining independence in 1918 after World War I.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.

example.hanzi: 很多年轻人认同这种环保的生活方式。
example.pinyin: hěn duō niánqīngrén rèntóng zhè zhǒng huánbǎo de shēnghuó fāngshì.
example.english: Many young people identify with this eco-friendly lifestyle.
example.fact: Social identity theory, developed by psychologist Henri Tajfel in the 1970s, showed that people form group loyalties and self-esteem around group membership so readily that even arbitrary, meaningless group labels assigned in an experiment were enough to trigger favoritism toward one's own group.

example.hanzi: 肯尼迪总统是在达拉斯遇刺的。

example.fact: Dallas grew from a small trading post founded in 1841 on the Trinity River into one of the largest US metro areas largely because of oil — the 1930 discovery of the vast East Texas Oil Field turned the region into a banking and business hub for the entire industry almost overnight.

example.hanzi: 新经理接手了一个烂摊子，花了半年才理清。

example.english: The new manager inherited a total mess and took half a year to sort it out.
example.fact: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster left behind one of the most literal 'shambles' in industrial history — the surrounding Exclusion Zone remains largely uninhabited decades later, though it has unexpectedly become a haven for wildlife like wolves and lynx, since the absence of humans has outweighed the radiation's harm to many species.

力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
以 originally depicted a person carrying or holding an object — the picture of putting something to use gave 以 its meaning 'with, by means of, in order to.'
Walk — going somewhere involves walking or moving.

example.fact: Free-diver Herbert Nitsch set the current 'no limits' depth record by descending to 214 meters on a single breath in 2007 — a feat requiring total physical and mental commitment, since a diver at that depth experiences pressure over 20 times greater than at the surface.

example.english: In spring, the cherry trees in the orchard are covered in blossoms.
example.fact: Japan's famous cherry blossom season is driven almost entirely by ornamental varieties bred for their flowers, not their fruit — most decorative sakura trees produce little or no edible cherries, while the cherries sold for eating come from a different set of cultivated varieties bred specifically for fruit production.

example.fact: Seasonal affective disorder, a form of depression tied to reduced sunlight in winter months, is thought to affect a meaningful share of people in temperate climates and is treated in part with bright light therapy — sitting in front of a specialized lightbox that mimics outdoor daylight intensity.

example.fact: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in June 1914 is the textbook example of a single incident provoking a chain reaction — within about five weeks, a web of alliances pulled nearly all of Europe's major powers into what became World War I.

example.english: Detroit was once the center of the American auto industry.
example.fact: Henry Ford's Highland Park plant in Detroit introduced the moving assembly line in 1913, cutting the time to build a Model T chassis from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes — a change so radical it reshaped not just car manufacturing but industrial production worldwide.

example.english: This isn't a movie plot — it's a real, living event.
example.fact: Coelacanths, a lineage of fish once thought to have gone extinct 66 million years ago alongside the dinosaurs, turned out to be very much alive when a living specimen was caught off the coast of South Africa in 1938, stunning scientists and earning the fish the nickname 'living fossil.'

日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

example.hanzi: 渔民们在黎明前就出海捕鱼了。
example.pinyin: yúmínmen zài límíng qián jiù chūhǎi bǔyú le.
example.english: The fishermen went out to sea to fish before dawn.
example.fact: At the Arctic Circle in midsummer, the sun never fully sets, so there is effectively no dawn at all for weeks at a time — a phenomenon called the midnight sun — while in midwinter the same region can go without a proper sunrise for an equally long stretch, a stark contrast most of the world never experiences.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
女 (woman) — 姆 names a woman who cares for children.
母 (mǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 姆's reading mǔ.
其 (a winnowing basket) — 斯 originally described splitting or separating grain from chaff.
斤 (an axe) — reinforced the action of splitting; 斯's original meaning faded as the character came to be used mainly for its sound in transliterations like 达拉斯 and 阿姆斯特丹.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'

example.hanzi: 阿姆斯特丹有数百座桥梁横跨运河。
example.pinyin: Āmǔsītèdān yǒu shùbǎi zuò qiáoliáng héngkuà yùnhé.
example.english: Amsterdam has hundreds of bridges crossing its canals.
example.fact: Much of Amsterdam is built on land reclaimed from water and rests on wooden piles driven deep into the soft soil beneath the city — some of the oldest buildings still stand on foundation poles that are several centuries old, and their slow decay is a real concern for preserving the historic city center today.

components.note: 页 (head) — 顽 originally described a quality of the head, i.e. stubbornness of mind.
元 (yuán) gives a sound fairly close to wán, sharing the rhyme.
囗 (an enclosure) — something firmly closed in is secure, tied to 固's meaning 'solid, firm.'
古 (gǔ) gives a rhyme close to gù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他对旧方法的坚持显得十分顽固。
example.pinyin: tā duì jiù fāngfǎ de jiānchí xiǎnde shífēn wángù.
example.english: His insistence on the old methods came across as very stubborn.
example.fact: Certain bacterial spores are so stubbornly resistant to destruction that some can survive boiling water and extreme drying — spores of Bacillus species have famously been revived in laboratory studies after being dormant for tens of thousands of years, and in some disputed claims, far longer.

components.note: 圣 is the simplified form of 聖, which combined an ear (耳, listening) and a mouth (口, speaking) above a standing figure — the image of someone who listens and speaks with special insight, giving 圣 its meaning 'holy, sacred.'
母 depicts a kneeling woman with two dots marking breasts — an image emphasizing nursing and motherhood, giving 母 its meaning 'mother.'

example.hanzi: 这幅画描绘的是圣母抱着婴儿的场景。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà miáohuì de shì shèngmǔ bào zhe yīng'ér de chǎngjǐng.
example.english: This painting depicts the scene of the Madonna holding an infant.
example.fact: Images of a mother goddess holding a child predate Christianity by thousands of years — the ancient Egyptian goddess Isis was frequently depicted nursing her son Horus, and many art historians argue this iconography directly influenced the visual conventions later used for paintings of the Madonna and Child.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 忽 describes a mental state, a sudden shift in attention.
勿 (wù) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading hū has diverged.
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 天空忽然变暗，下起了暴雨。
example.pinyin: tiānkōng hūrán biàn àn, xià qǐ le bàoyǔ.
example.english: The sky suddenly turned dark, and a heavy rain began to fall.
example.fact: Flash floods can turn a dry desert canyon into a raging torrent in a matter of minutes, even under a clear sky overhead, because the triggering storm may be falling many miles upstream — a hazard that makes canyons like those in Utah's Zion National Park especially dangerous to hikers caught off guard.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — 鲜 originally described fresh fish or meat.
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 鲜.
艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'

example.hanzi: 他每周都会给妈妈送一束鲜花。
example.pinyin: tā měi zhōu dōu huì gěi māma sòng yì shù xiānhuā.
example.english: He gives his mother a bouquet of fresh flowers every week.
example.fact: The Netherlands exports more cut flowers than any other country in the world, and the Aalsmeer flower auction near Amsterdam is one of the largest flower markets on Earth, trading tens of millions of flowers and plants on a typical day before many are flown out to florists worldwide within 24 hours.

components.note: 免 originally pictured a person removing a ceremonial cap or helmet — the act of taking something off gave 免 its meaning 'to remove, excuse from,' and later 'to avoid.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 出门带把伞，免得下雨淋湿了。
example.pinyin: chūmén dài bǎ sǎn, miǎnde xiàyǔ lín shī le.
example.english: Bring an umbrella when you go out, so you won't get soaked if it rains.
example.fact: Lightning rods, invented by Benjamin Franklin in 1752, work by giving electrical current a low-resistance path to the ground, so a rod-equipped building is struck 'safely' instead of the current arcing destructively through the structure itself — a simple design that still protects most modern skyscrapers today.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
千 modifies the character 人 (person) with an added stroke — using a human figure to stand for a large round number gave 千 its meaning 'thousand.'

example.hanzi: 这场演唱会吸引了上千名观众。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng yǎnchànghuì xīyǐn le shàngqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This concert attracted upwards of a thousand spectators.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army buried near China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, contains upwards of 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features — archaeologists believe many more may still lie unexcavated in the surrounding pits discovered since 1974.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
目 (eye) — supervising, 督's meaning, involves watching closely.
叔 (shū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading dū has diverged.
彳 pictures a person's legs walking.
走 (to walk/run) reinforces the idea of movement, giving 徒 its meanings 'on foot' and 'a follower who walks in someone's footsteps.'

example.hanzi: 他的祖父母是虔诚的基督徒。
example.pinyin: tā de zǔfùmǔ shì qiánchéng de Jīdūtú.
example.english: His grandparents are devout Christians.
example.fact: Christianity was still a minority, often persecuted faith within the Roman Empire for its first three centuries, until Emperor Constantine's Edict of Milan in 313 AD legalized it, and by the end of that same century it had become the empire's official state religion under Theodosius I.

components.note: 力 (strength) — relates to 办's meaning 'to handle, manage, do,' something accomplished through effort.
八 (bā) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from bàn.
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 这位律师办案经验丰富，从不轻易放弃。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi lǜshī bàn'àn jīngyàn fēngfù, cóng bù qīngyì fàngqì.
example.english: This lawyer has extensive experience handling cases and never gives up easily.
example.fact: DNA evidence, first used to help solve a criminal case in England in 1986, revolutionized how cases are handled — the same techniques have since been used by projects like the Innocence Project to exonerate hundreds of wrongfully convicted people, some of whom had already spent decades in prison.

components.note: 贝 (money) — 贩 relates to trading for profit.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound close to fàn, differing only in tone.
买 (to buy) — 卖 (to sell) is the flip side of buying, the other half of a transaction.
买 (mǎi) gives a sound very close to mài, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 当地政府严厉打击非法贩卖野生动物的行为。
example.pinyin: dāngdì zhèngfǔ yánlì dǎjī fēifǎ fànmài yěshēng dòngwù de xíngwéi.
example.english: The local government is cracking down hard on the illegal trafficking of wild animals.
example.fact: The illegal wildlife trade is estimated by conservation groups to be worth billions of dollars a year, making it one of the largest illicit trades globally alongside drugs and arms — pangolins alone are believed to be the most trafficked mammal on Earth, prized largely for their scales in traditional medicine markets.

components.note: 入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
犭 (dog) on the left represents a guard dog.
讠 (speech) suggests an accusation or a legal case being spoken.
犬 (dog) on the right completes the scene, giving 狱 its meaning 'prison, lawsuit.'

example.hanzi: 他因为诈骗罪被判入狱五年。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi zhàpiànzuì bèi pàn rùyù wǔ nián.
example.english: He was sentenced to five years in prison for fraud.
example.fact: The United States has the highest documented incarceration rate of any country in the world, holding roughly 20% of the world's prisoners despite having only about 4% of the global population, according to figures widely cited by criminal justice researchers.

components.note: 人 (a man) — the figure straining upward.
止 (feet) — standing up on his feet, or toes, to look into the distance, the image of anticipation giving 企 its meaning 'to look forward to, hope for' and, by extension, 'enterprise' (企业).
鸟 (bird) — 鹅 names a type of bird, the goose.
我 (wǒ) gives a sound distantly related to 鹅's reading é, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 南极的企鹅群在冰面上排成长队行走。
example.pinyin: Nánjí de qǐ'é qún zài bīngmiàn shàng pái chéng chángduì xíngzǒu.
example.english: The colony of penguins in Antarctica walks in a long line across the ice.
example.fact: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 meters and hold their breath for over 20 minutes while hunting, thanks to a slowed heart rate and specialized hemoglobin that lets their bodies keep functioning on far less oxygen than most air-breathing animals could tolerate.

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
口 (mouth) — 喻 relates to explaining something through speech.
俞 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, sharing the same rhyme and a related tone.

example.hanzi: 老师用了一个生动的比喻来解释这个概念。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī yòng le yí gè shēngdòng de bǐyù lái jiěshì zhège gàiniàn.
example.english: The teacher used a vivid metaphor to explain this concept.
example.fact: Cognitive linguists George Lakoff and Mark Johnson argued in their influential 1980 book 'Metaphors We Live By' that metaphor isn't just a literary decoration but a fundamental way human thought is structured — for example, the pervasive metaphor of 'time is money' shapes how English speakers talk about spending, wasting, and saving time, not just cash.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 湖 names a body of water, a lake.
胡 (hú) gives the sound — an exact match with 湖.
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他们在湖边搭了一个帐篷过夜。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài húbiān dā le yí gè zhàngpéng guòyè.
example.english: They set up a tent by the lakeside to spend the night.
example.fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia, the deepest lake in the world at over 1,600 meters, holds roughly 20% of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth's surface — more than all five of North America's Great Lakes combined.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
立 (to stand) — 旁 relates to standing to the side of something.
方 (fāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 旁.

example.hanzi: 无论遇到什么困难，她都会陪在他身旁。
example.pinyin: wúlùn yù dào shénme kùnnán, tā dōu huì péi zài tā shēnpáng.
example.english: No matter what difficulties arise, she will stay by his side.
example.fact: Emperor penguins and many other cold-climate animals use a behavior called huddling, pressing close against the animals beside them, to conserve body heat so effectively that the center of a huddle can be around 20 degrees Celsius warmer than the surrounding air during Antarctic winters.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 飞机因为天气原因中途改变了航线。
example.pinyin: fēijī yīnwèi tiānqì yuányīn zhōngtú gǎibiàn le hángxiàn.
example.english: The plane changed its route midway due to weather conditions.
example.fact: The Apollo 13 mission became one of the most famous mid-flight crises in space history when an oxygen tank exploded roughly 56 hours into the flight, forcing the crew to abandon their moon landing and improvise a survival plan using the lunar module as a lifeboat for the trip back to Earth.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
王 here is a variant of 玉 (jade), appearing once on each side of the character.
刂 (knife) — cutting a piece of jade in two, symbolizing a division into groups, gave 班 its meaning 'class, group.'

example.hanzi: 为了赶项目进度，团队这周每天都要加班。
example.pinyin: wèile gǎn xiàngmù jìndù, tuánduì zhè zhōu měitiān dōu yào jiābān.
example.english: To meet the project deadline, the team has to work overtime every day this week.
example.fact: Japan has a specific legal and medical term, karoshi, meaning 'death from overwork,' recognized since the late 1980s to describe fatal strokes, heart attacks, or suicides linked directly to extreme work hours — the government now publishes an annual white paper tracking related labor cases.

components.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
口 (mouth) — 含 originally meant to hold something in the mouth.
今 (jīn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading hán has diverged.

example.hanzi: 这份套餐包含早餐和晚餐。
example.pinyin: zhè fèn tàocān bāohán zǎocān hé wǎncān.
example.english: This package includes breakfast and dinner.
example.fact: The observable universe is estimated to include roughly two trillion galaxies, according to a 2016 analysis of deep Hubble Space Telescope images — a figure roughly ten times higher than earlier estimates, showing how much even 'complete' astronomical surveys can still be missing.

components.note: A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'
厤 (relating to the sequence of time) — 历 relates to history and the calendar
力 (lì) gives the sound — 历 is pronounced lì, an exact match
山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 亚历山大大帝在三十岁前就征服了大半个已知世界。
example.pinyin: Yàlìshāndà dàdì zài sānshí suì qián jiù zhēngfú le dàbàn gè yǐzhī shìjiè.
example.english: Alexander the Great had conquered most of the known world before he turned thirty.
example.fact: Alexander the Great founded more than 20 cities across his empire, many named Alexandria after himself — the most famous, in Egypt, later became home to one of the ancient world's greatest libraries and a major center of scholarship for centuries after his death in 323 BC.
